title: What Are Your Thoughts on Rainer Werner Fassbinder?

commenti.body:
For me one of the most striking aspects of Fassbinder’s body of work is how quirky his actresses looked. Because another example of this is Almodovar, I wonder if this was due to the fact that Fassbinder, as a gay man, did not have quite the same “male gaze” that drive the casting decisions of most other male filmmakers.

Another thing I love is his propensity for scenes where a snobbish character feigns politeness and interest in a person, while obviously looking down on them. There’s a black humor in this. I also feel that in Fassbinder’s depiction of cold, unfeeling societies there is an affinity with Aki Kaurismäki, yet I don’t think I have even seen Fassbinder named among Kaurismäki’s inspirations.

> how did Fassbinder manage to do so much in a short period of time?

Amphetamines.

> Where should I start with Fassbinder?

Marriage of Maria Braun and Ali: Fear Eats the Soul are relatively approachable. They’re closer to regular melodramas. Then I’d suggest moving onto:

* Chinese Roulette
* Despair
* In a Year of 13 Moons
* The Bitter Tears of Petra Von Kant
* Lola
* Fox and His Friends

These start to have some bizarre story elements and/or some cases sort of gimmicks which can make following the story difficult. If you’re still excited, keep going!

Alternate approach: Start with Water Drops on Burning Rocks [2000], directed by Ozon, based on a play by Fassbinder. Very Fassbinder-esque, but I think the pacing and cinematography might be more accessible to modern audiences.

>I only heard of The Marriage Of Maria Braun and Berlin Alexanderplatz and that Maria Braun is his masterpiece and Alexanderplatz is a very good Miniseries

Berlin Alexanderplatz is the best thing he has ever done in my opinion. 

Like others have said Ali: Fear Eats the Soul is a good starting point.
